q.t: Find sin 30°.
q.e: Half of an equilateral triangle of side 2 has hypotenuse 2 and side 1 opposite 30°.

q.t: Find tan 45°.
q.e: A 45° right triangle is isosceles, so opposite = adjacent.

q.t: Find sin 60°.
q.e: In the half-equilateral triangle (1, √3, 2), the side opposite 60° is √3.

q.t: Find cos 0°.
q.e: As the angle shrinks to 0°, the adjacent side becomes the whole hypotenuse.

q.t: What is tan 90°?
q.e: tan 90° = sin 90°/cos 90° = 1/0, and we cannot divide by zero.

q.t: Find sin 90° + cos 90°.
q.e: sin 90° = 1 and cos 90° = 0.

q.t: Find sec 60°.
q.e: cos 60° = 1/2, and sec is its reciprocal.

q.t: Find cosec 45°.
Find tan 30°.
q.e: In the (1, √3, 2) triangle, opposite 30° is 1 and adjacent is √3.

q.t: Find 2 sin 30° cos 30°.
Find sin 60° cos 30° + cos 60° sin 30°.
Find 3 tan² 45° − sin² 60° + cos² 30°.
Find 4 cos² 60° + 3 sec² 30° − tan² 45°.
If sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A − B) = 1 (A, B acute), find A in degrees.
q.e: A + B = 90° and A − B = 0°, so A = B = 45°.

q.t: If tan 2A = √3 (2A acute), find A in degrees.
Find (1 − tan² 30°)/(1 + tan² 30°).
Find sin 45° cos 45° + tan² 60°.
If 2 cos θ = 1 (θ acute), find θ in degrees.
q.e: cos θ = 1/2, and cos 60° = 1/2.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at B with ∠A = 30° and AC = 20 cm. Find BC.
q.e: BC is opposite 30°: BC = AC sin 30° = 20 × 1/2.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at B with ∠C = 45° and AB = 6 cm. Find AC.
q.e: A 45° right triangle is isosceles, so BC = 6 too; AC = √(36 + 36) = 6√2.

q.t: If sin(2θ − 10°) = cos 60° (θ acute), find θ in degrees.
If cos(A − B) = √3/2 and sin(A + B) = 1, find A in degrees.
Find 2 sin² 30° + cot² 30° − sec² 45°.
For which acute or zero angle A is sin 2A = 2 sin A?
q.e: Try them: only at 0° do both sides equal 0. At 30°, sin 60° ≈ 0.87 but 2 sin 30° = 1.

q.t: Find x if x tan 45° cos 60° = sin 60° cot 60°.
A ladder makes 60° with the ground and its foot is 2.5 m from the wall. Find the ladder’s length.
q.e: cos 60° = foot distance ÷ ladder: 2.5 ÷ 1/2.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at C with ∠A = 30° and AB = 10 cm. Find AC.
q.e: AC is adjacent to A: AC = AB cos 30° = 10 × √3/2.

q.t: Find 4 cos³ 30° − 3 cos 30°.
Using sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B with A = 45°, B = 30°, find sin 75°.
If √3 tan θ = 3 sin θ (θ acute), find sin² θ − cos² θ.
q.e: Divide by sin θ: √3/cos θ = 3, so cos θ = 1/√3. Then cos² θ = 1/3, sin² θ = 2/3.

q.t: If sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A − 2B) = 1 (A, B acute), find A in degrees.
Find (sec² 45° + cot² 60° + 3 tan² 30°)/(cosec² 30° − tan² 60°).
If θ = 30°, find 2 tan θ/(1 − tan² θ).
If sin(A − B) = 1/2 and cos(A + B) = 0 (A, B acute), find B in degrees.
q.e: A − B = 30° and A + B = 90°: subtract to get 2B = 60°.

q.t: If cos θ/(1 − sin θ) + cos θ/(1 + sin θ) = 4 (θ acute), find θ in degrees.
q.e: The sum is 2cos θ/(1 − sin² θ) = 2/cos θ = 4, so cos θ = 1/2.

q.t: A diagonal AC = 12 cm of rectangle ABCD makes 30° with AB. Find the area of the rectangle.
q.e: AB = 12 cos 30° = 6√3 and BC = 12 sin 30° = 6, so area = 36√3.

q.t: Find cos² 30° cos² 45° + 4 sec² 60° + ½ cos² 90° − 2 tan² 60°.
Find 3 sin 30° − 4 sin³ 30°.
ΔPQR is right-angled at Q with PQ = 4 cm and QR = 4√3 cm. Find ∠PRQ in degrees.
q.e: tan R = PQ/QR = 1/√3, so ∠R = 30° (and ∠P = 60°).

q.t: Using sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B with A = 45°, B = 30°, find sin 15°.
